newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CEZ CONTINUES RAPID RISE ON PRAGUE BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: CEZ CONTINUES RAPID RISE ON PRAGUE BOURSE.

text.p: Czech utility CEZ a.s. continued irs rapid rise at the daily price fixing on the Prague Stock Exchange, though analysts said the shares may be reaching a peak as questions over its revenues linger.
CEZ was up 50 crowns at 1,260 in the early minutes of the bourse's continue trading session, which begins at 1130 a.m. (1030 GMT).
"In comparison with other European power generators, CEZ is still sell at an attractive P/E," said Bram Burning of the Brni Broker Group.

But, he warned: "On a purely speculative basis, our traders would buy up to 1,200 crowns. We, however, are more pessimistic about a company with declining earnings and no dividends, and above 1,100 crowns our recommendation is to hold."
He added: "Fundamentally, CEZ will see lower profits for the next 2-3 years due to increased depreciation and interest costs resulting from its huge investments."
The Czech government still regulates energy prices and has shown little willingness to fully free prices in the short-term.
